question: Who popularised the movement of Theosophical Society in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Annie Besant**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Annie Besant** was a prominent British socialist, theosophist, and supporter of Indian self-rule.

• She was instrumental in popularizing the **Theosophical Society** in India through her extensive lectures and writings.

• Annie Besant was a key figure in the Indian nationalist movement and even served as the president of the Indian National Congress in 1917.

• Her efforts significantly contributed to the spread of theosophical ideas and the revival of Hindu religious and cultural identities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Theosophical Society**

• The Theosophical Society was founded in New York City in 1875 by Helena Petrovna Blavatsky, Henry Steel Olcott, and William Quan Judge.

• The society's main objectives include the formation of a universal brotherhood of humanity, the study of comparative religion, philosophy, and science, and the investigation of the unexplained laws of nature and the powers latent in humans.

• Theosophy seeks to explore the divine wisdom underlying all religions and philosophies, promoting the idea of universal brotherhood and the interconnectedness of all life.

• **Annie Besant's Contribution to Indian Society**

• Annie Besant arrived in India in 1893 and became actively involved in the Theosophical Society's activities.

• She established the Central Hindu College (later became Banaras Hindu University) and played a significant role in the Indian Home Rule Movement.

• In addition to her theosophical work, Besant was a staunch advocate for social reforms, including women's rights, education, and labor rights.

• **Indian National Congress (INC)**

• The INC was founded in 1885 and became the principal leader of the Indian independence movement.

• Annie Besant's presidency of the INC in 1917 marked a significant moment, as she was the first woman to hold the position.

• Her leadership helped to galvanize support for India's self-rule and brought international attention to the Indian independence struggle.
